title: Infinite Progression: Balancing Exponential Cost Curves and Simulated Infinity
subtitle: This guide deconstructs cost scaling and milestone thresholds in clicker/idle games to implement sustainable 'simulated infinity.' By combining non-linear cost growth with periodic system unlocks and prestige mechanics, developers can maintain player engagement without triggering late-game collapse, offering a high-execution framework for solving retention issues in pseudo-infinite loops.

breakdown.title: Constructing Cost Curves
bullets: Exponential is the default solution: cost = base × r^level (where r typically ranges from 1.07 to 1.15)
Segment the growth rate r: use a lower r early for immediate gratification and a higher r later to extend the progression curve
Avoid exponential scaling for rewards: keep rewards sub-exponential or segmented to prevent the economy from collapsing overnight

breakdown.title: Simulated Infinity (Better for Operations)
bullets: Slice infinity into stages using milestones: unlock new systems or dimensions upon reaching specific thresholds
Prestige/Rebirth: Reset partial progress in exchange for permanent bonuses, accelerating growth for the next cycle
Leaderboards/Seasons: Transform infinite goals into short-term, comparable cycles to maintain competitive pressure

breakdown.title: Psychological Thresholds
bullets: Players can accept waiting, but cannot accept not seeing visible progress
Provide visible upgrades every 30~90 seconds (via numbers, effects, or unlocks)
Implement a unit system for large numbers to prevent the UI from becoming unreadable gibberish
